claims.question: Q1
claims.claim: For Local Services Ads in the US and Canada, Google says every inbound call that comes in through the Google forwarding number is recorded.
claims.quote: Note that in the US and Canada, all inbound calls from customers via the Google forwarding number are recorded by Google to improve quality and support policies and research
claims.note: Page shows no date. Same page says recordings are not available for health care verticals or tax specialists.

claims.question: Q1
claims.claim: Google's Local Services data page says all calls, emails and texts delivered through Google may be monitored or recorded, including new and follow-up calls between consumers and providers.
claims.quote: All phone calls, emails, and text-based communications delivered through Google may be monitored or recorded to detect spam or unauthorized behavior and to improve quality, support policies, and research, subject to Google's privacy policy.
claims.note: Section headed 'Your Data in North America'.

claims.question: Q1
claims.claim: For consumers outside North America, the Local Services data page lists the data Google keeps from a routed call as the phone number, date and time, and duration, and does not mention recordings in that section.
claims.quote: Google will retain the consumer's phone number (if available), the date and time of the communication, the duration of the call, and the context of the text message
claims.note: The absence of a recording statement is my observation from reading the section, not a statement by Google that recording does not happen.

claims.question: Q1
claims.claim: Playback of Local Services phone lead recordings in the lead inbox is offered for the US only.
claims.quote: Listen to phone lead recordings (US only)

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Google Ads now has the call recording setting turned on by default so Google can use AI to qualify call leads.
claims.quote: The call recording setting is now enabled by default to allow for AI-powered lead qualification.
claims.note: Page shows no date. Search Engine Journal dated the change April 21, 2026.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: The default stays off for accounts that previously turned recording off and for businesses Google identified as healthcare or financial services.
claims.quote: Call recording will remain turned off if you previously turned it off, or if your business was identified as operating in healthcare or financial services.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Google Ads call recording applies to calls made directly to call ads, call assets and calls from website visits, but not calls from location assets.
claims.quote: Only calls made directly to call ads, call assets or calls from website visits are eligible; calls from your location assets are not supported for recording at this time.
claims.note: The older 'Play your call recordings' page (answer 9882109) lists calls to a website call conversion tag as an unsupported call source. The pages differ; the newer one lists calls from website visits as eligible.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Recording requires the call to flow through a Google Forwarding Number, which requires call reporting to be on in the account.
claims.quote: Calls must flow through a Google Forwarding Number. This requires call reporting to be turned on in your account settings.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Google Ads call recording is currently limited to calls involving phone numbers in the United States and Canada.
claims.quote: Currently, call recording and AI-qualified conversions are only available for calls involving phone numbers in the United States and Canada.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: When recording is on, Google says all calls are recorded and evaluated by AI, and only calls the AI qualifies count as conversions.
claims.quote: Primary signal (call recording): If call recording is on, all calls will be recorded and evaluated by AI. Only qualified calls will count as conversions.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Google emailed advertisers that from July 1, 2026 an empty Call recording setting would automatically become Yes.
claims.quote: Starting July 01, 2026, if you haven't made a selection for your "Call recording" setting, it will automatically default to "Yes".
claims.note: Secondary source quoting Google's email to advertisers; Google's help page does not show the July 1 date.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: An older Google Ads help page describes recording as a small percentage of calls from call-only ads or call assets for some US advertisers, tied to accepting the Call and Messaging Ads Terms.
claims.quote: Google monitors and records a small percentage of phone calls that are initiated by a call-only ad or call asset for some advertisers in the United States
claims.note: Older wording that is still live; it conflicts with the newer default-on, all-calls wording on answer 16913427.

claims.question: Q3
claims.claim: For Google Ads calls, the caller hears a short automated message at the start saying the conversation will be recorded for quality purposes.
claims.quote: Callers will hear a short automated message at the beginning of the call notifying them that the conversation will be recorded for quality purposes.

claims.question: Q3
claims.claim: The older Google Ads page says the caller hears a short message that the call will be recorded by Google for quality assurance.
claims.quote: The user will hear a short message informing them that the call will be recorded by Google for quality assurance.

claims.question: Q3
claims.claim: For Local Services Ads in the US and Canada, the caller hears a pre-recorded notice, and the business then hears a 'Call from Google' message.
claims.quote: (and customers are notified of this by a pre-recorded message immediately before you hear the “Call from Google” notification)

claims.question: Q3
claims.claim: Google says the business may not hear the 'Call from Google' message if the business number has call forwarding or VoIP set up.
claims.quote: Note: You may not hear the “Call from Google” message if you have any type of call forwarding or VoIP set up on the business phone number on your Local Services account.

claims.question: Q3
claims.claim: A State Bar of Wisconsin ethics counsel article quoted a 2020 marketer's description of the two whisper messages: the caller hears that the call is not confidential, and the law firm hears that the call is recorded and may not be attorney-client privileged.
claims.quote: Caller will hear: ‘Google and its partners may record or return all calls for quality and research purposes, subject to our privacy policies. This call is not confidential.’ Recipient (law firm) will hear: ‘Call from Google. This call is recorded and may not be attorney-client privileged.’
claims.note: Quoted second-hand from a marketer; the author's own Dec 2020 test call heard only 'not confidential' (footnote 6). Wording may have changed since. Google's Ads help does not say what the business hears on a recorded Google Ads (non-LSA) call.

claims.question: Q4
claims.claim: For Local Services in North America, Google says call recordings and messages are kept up to 180 days before they are destroyed.
claims.quote: Call recordings and messages are retained up to 180 days before they are destroyed.

claims.question: Q4
claims.claim: For legal verticals in Local Services, Google sets a shorter retention of 60 days.
claims.quote: Recordings and messages in legal verticals are retained for 60 days.
claims.note: This sentence also shows Google treats legal as a vertical in which recordings are made and kept.

claims.question: Q4
claims.claim: For Google Ads, a recorded call stays playable in the Call Details report for 30 days after the call date.
claims.quote: Recorded calls are available for 30 days after the date of the call.
claims.note: Older page written before the 2026 default change; the newer settings page (answer 16913427) states no retention period, so whether 30 days still applies is not confirmed. No separate period for legal is stated for Google Ads.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: In Google Ads, users with Admin or Standard access (including MCC users) can play recordings once enabled.
claims.quote: MCC and direct users with Admin or direct users with Standard access will be able to play recordings, once enabled.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google Ads recordings can be played only inside the Google Ads interface and cannot be downloaded.
claims.quote: Call recording is only available using the Google Ads UI and the recordings are not available for download.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: In Local Services, providers may review call recordings, and Google says it does not monitor or control how providers use them.
claims.quote: Providers may review call recordings in order to track conversations. Google does not monitor or control how providers use the recordings.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says it reviews Local Services emails, texts or call recordings on a limited basis for a list of purposes.
claims.quote: Google reviews emails, texts, or call recordings routed through Google’s system on a limited basis for the following purposes:
claims.note: The list that follows includes: resolve billing disputes; bill Local Services advertisers for leads; enforce policies; detect spam and unauthorized behavior; collect customer feedback; product improvement; monitor customer and provider experience.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says its AI-qualified call leads feature uses Google AI to evaluate call recordings to judge the quality of the conversation.
claims.quote: AI-qualified call leads use Google AI to evaluate call recordings (the call recording setting must be turned on) to determine the actual quality of the conversation.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says Call Details reports now show an AI-generated summary of each call and hashtags such as #HighIntent.
claims.quote: Your Call Details reports will now feature a concise AI-generated summary of the call and specific hashtags (for example, “#HighIntent,” “#ConsultationScheduled”) to help you understand customer needs at a glance.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google states it uses Google Ads recordings to evaluate lead quality, monitor spam and fraud, and improve conversion reporting accuracy.
claims.quote: Recordings are used to evaluate lead quality, monitor spam and fraud, and improve the accuracy of your conversion reporting.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: The older Google Ads page says information from calls is anonymized and used only to detect unauthorized activity and assess quality in aggregate.
claims.quote: Information taken from calls is anonymized and only used to detect unauthorized activity and assess quality in aggregate.
claims.note: Older wording; it sits beside the newer AI-classification use and may be superseded.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: The older Google Ads page says recordings are not used for ad targeting.
claims.quote: Recordings will not be used for ad targeting purposes.
claims.note: Older wording; the Local Services terms say information from recorded communications may be used as Content (next claim).

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: The US Local Services terms say Google may use information collected from recorded communications in line with its Privacy Policy and as 'Content' under the terms.
claims.quote: Google may use information collected under this paragraph in compliance with its Privacy Policy and as Content under Section 3 above.
claims.note: Version TC-US-2025-03 as fetched Oct 13, 2026. I did not confirm whether a newer version exists.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: A law firm marketing site reports that, under Local Services terms effective April 2025, Google reserves the right to use the content of calls and messages routed through LSAs to generate ad copy and train its systems.
claims.quote: Under terms that took effect April 2025, Google also reserves the right to use the content of phone calls and messages routed through LSAs to generate ad copy and train its systems.
claims.note: Secondary and a marketer's reading. I did not find this wording in the primary US terms version TC-US-2025-03, so treat as unverified against Google's text.

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: A Google Ads advertiser can turn recording on or off in Account settings under the Call ads drop-down, in the Call recording field.
claims.quote: Under “Call recording”, select On or Off.

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: Turning recording off stops the AI from analyzing calls, and conversions fall back to call duration.
claims.quote: Note: Disabling call recording will prevent the AI from analyzing conversations for lead quality. In this case, the system will fall back to using call duration to measure conversions.

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: Google says the advertiser can turn off call recording at any time.
claims.quote: How to turn off call recording: You can turn off call recording at any time by following these instructions.

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: Under the older terms, an advertiser that cannot take part for legal or regulatory reasons is told to contact Google to request an exemption from monitoring and recording.
claims.quote: If you have questions about eligibility or can't participate in call recording for legal or regulatory reasons, contact Google to request an exemption from monitoring and recording.

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: Under the older terms, declining to accept the Call and Messaging Ads Terms means the account cannot create or edit call ads and assets.
claims.quote: If you choose not to accept, your account will not be able to create or edit call ads and assets.

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: The Call Ads Supplemental Terms say an advertiser that declines them may not be able to use features that enable communications such as click-to-call.
claims.quote: If you choose not to accept these Supplemental Terms, you may not be able to use Program features that enable Communications (“Communication Features”).

claims.question: Q7
claims.claim: Google Ads skips recording by default for sensitive industries such as specific healthcare or financial services, unless the advertiser accepts the Call Ads Supplemental Terms; legal services are not named on this page.
claims.quote: Sensitive Verticals: To protect user privacy, call recording is automatically skipped for advertisers in sensitive industries, like specific healthcare or financial services unless explicitly enabled by the advertiser by accepting Call Ads Supplemental Terms.
claims.note: The word 'like' means the list may not be complete, but legal services are not named anywhere on the page. I found no Google page that lists legal as excluded from Ads call recording.

claims.question: Q7
claims.claim: In Local Services, Google says recordings and messages are not available for health care verticals or tax specialists.
claims.quote: Note: Call recordings and messages aren't available for health care verticals or tax specialists.
claims.note: Legal is not listed; see the claim that sets 60-day retention for legal verticals.

claims.question: Q7
claims.claim: The Call Ads Supplemental Terms tell HIPAA covered entities and business associates not to accept them and to ask Google for exclusion from monitoring and recording.
claims.quote: please reach out to your Google account representative or Google support to request exclusion from monitoring and recording of Communications.
claims.note: The exclusion path is for HIPAA entities; no equivalent path for lawyers is stated.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The North Carolina State Bar Ethics Committee published Proposed 2021 FEO 5 on pay-per-lead advertising, which would have found participation prejudicial to the administration of justice under Rule 8.4(d).
claims.quote: Proposed 2021 FEO 5 concluded that the structure of the advertising program renders a lawyer’s participation in it prejudicial to the administration of justice in violation of Rule 8.4(d)
claims.note: The article's title names Google's LSA program; the body describes the program as pay-per-lead without naming Google. The proposed opinion's own text was not retrieved.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The Ethics Committee withdrew Proposed 2021 FEO 5 at its April 2022 meeting, so it never became a formal opinion.
claims.quote: Therefore, at its meeting in April 2022, the Ethics Committee withdrew Proposed 2021 FEO 5.
claims.note: Status: withdrawn, per the bar's own article, which is still posted on ncbar.gov as of Oct 13, 2026.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The Committee concluded the recordings are not uniquely vulnerable to harmful third-party disclosure and that a platform-specific opinion would not benefit the profession or consumers.
claims.quote: the recordings at issue are not uniquely vulnerable to harmful third-party disclosures, and that adopting a specific ethics opinion related to this particular advertising platform would not benefit the legal profession or the consumers

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The bar says the confidentiality duty applies only within an attorney-client relationship, so a lawyer should take care that a potential client does not become a Rule 1.18 prospective client.
claims.quote: lawyers need to remember that the duty of confidentiality set out in the Rules of Professional Conduct only applies in the context of an attorney-client relationship.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The bar suggests staff who answer calls forwarded by an ad program tell callers that the advertising company can record the call and it will not be confidential.
claims.quote: Because you called us by clicking on an advertisement, the advertising company is able to record this call and anything you say will not be confidential.
claims.note: Suggested script from the bar's article; it continues 'But if you will give me your phone number, I will be happy to call you back on a private line.'

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: State Bar of Wisconsin ethics counsel (Aviva Meridian Kaiser) wrote in January 2021 that, unless prospective clients give informed consent, a lawyer violates the duty of confidentiality by authorizing Google to record LSA calls and disclose information to third parties.
claims.quote: Consequently, unless the prospective clients give informed consent, the lawyer violates the duty of confidentiality by authorizing Google to access, monitor and record phone calls and text messages, and by authorizing Google to disclose information to third parties.
claims.note: Status: an ethics counsel article in the bar's newsletter (Inside Track), not a formal ethics opinion; still posted as of Oct 13, 2026. Written about the 2017 terms (TC-US-2017-08) and 2020 whisper wording; Google's terms have changed since.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The same article concluded the LSA does not include an adequate disclaimer to avoid creating a prospective-client relationship.
claims.quote: The LSA does not include an adequate disclaimer: the message does not, from the perspective of a layperson – not a lawyer – make it clear that there is no prospective lawyer-client relationship.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The article says the whisper message does not give the information needed for informed consent under Wisconsin's rule.
claims.quote: The “whisper message” does not communicate adequate information and explanation about the material risks of authorizing Google to access, monitor and record phone calls and text messages.

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: By accepting the Call Ads Supplemental Terms, the advertiser says it has given notice to its agents, employees and any other participant that communications may be monitored or recorded by Google and that recordings may be used by Google, the advertiser or an approved third party.
claims.quote: You have provided notice to your agents, employees, and any other party that may participate in the Communications that (a) these Communications may be monitored or recorded by Google, and (b) such recordings may be used by Google, you, or a third party approved by Google or you
claims.note: The terms page says they currently apply to advertisers in the United States. Page shows no date.

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: The same terms say the advertiser has obtained express consent from those people to the monitoring, recording and use.
claims.quote: and you have obtained their express consent to such monitoring and recording and use.

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: An advertiser acting for a third party must give that third party the same notice, obtain its express consent, and require it to pass notice and get consent from its own people.
claims.quote: you have required the third party to provide such notice to, and obtain consent from, its agents, employees, and any other party that may participate in the Communications.

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: The terms also require the advertiser and others on the communication to comply with the Telephone Consumer Protection Act and other applicable laws.
claims.quote: You and any other party that may participate in the Communications will comply with the Telephone Consumer Protection Act and other applicable laws when using the Communication Features

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: Google's help page says that by using call recording the advertiser agrees to the Call Ads Supplemental Terms and acknowledges it has given notice to agents, employees and other participants.
claims.quote: By using call recording features, you agree to the Call Ads Supplemental Terms and you acknowledge that you have provided notice to your agents, employees, and any other party that may participate in the Communications.

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: The US Local Services terms require the provider to obtain the permissions local law requires, notify its Team that communications may be recorded, and obtain their consent.
claims.quote: You also will obtain the necessary permissions required under local law and will notify your Team that these communications may be recorded and will obtain their consent to the recordings.
claims.note: This clause covers the provider's Team, not callers; the caller notice is Google's own recorded message.

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: By using Local Services, the provider authorizes Google and its affiliates and agents to access, monitor and record calls, texts, live chat and other communications.
claims.quote: You authorize Google, its affiliates, and their agents to access, monitor, and record telephone calls, text messages, live chat, and other communications initiated through the Programs (e.g., click-to-call ads).

leads.question: Q8
leads.what: Florida law firm press release (May 29, 2025) arguing Google's 2025 Local Services terms may conflict with Florida Bar rules 4-1.6, 4-7.13 and 4-7.14; advocacy, not a Florida Bar document.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Page returned HTTP 403 to my fetch; seen only in search results.

leads.question: Q8
leads.what: Connecticut Bar Association Informal Opinion 13-08 (June 19, 2013) on a pay-per-call service that records and stores prospective-client calls; about a vendor, not Google.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Third-party summary only; not opened, and the Connecticut Bar's own copy was not reached. Not about Google ads.

leads.question: Q8
leads.what: NYC Bar Formal Opinion 2025-6 on AI tools that record, transcribe and summarize client conversations; adjacent to Google AI analysis of calls but not about Google ads. A city bar, not a state bar.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Not opened; off topic for ad-platform recording.

leads.question: Q8
leads.what: North Carolina Lawyers Weekly story (Aug 16, 2021) on the proposed opinion; could give the proposed opinion's original wording.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Not opened; the bar's own article was used instead.

leads.question: Q8
leads.what: Orange County Bar Association 'Ethically Speaking' column, Dec 2021, on recording initial client calls (county bar, not state bar).

leads.question: Q9
leads.what: Anthony Higman X post on the Call and Messaging Ads terms (PPC marketer reaction: burden of notice and express consent now on advertisers); not a lawyer or law firm.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Opened, but it is one marketer's post with no date in the fetched text, and its content is covered by the quoted terms in the Q10 claims.

leads.question: Q9
leads.what: Local Lead Labs (Skool) post, Apr 28, 2026, on an 'LSA Privilege Trap' for law firms, with 2 comments; marketer-run community.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Opened, but the fetched text is truncated ('See more') and the comments were not shown, so I had no quotable statement.

leads.question: Q9
leads.what: Possible Reddit threads (r/LawFirm, r/Lawyertalk) and Google Ads Community threads about law firms and recorded LSA or Ads calls.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Reddit is blocked to the search tool and returned HTTP 403 to curl; no thread URL was found by search.

leads.question: Q5
leads.what: Search Engine Land piece on Google asserting rights over advertiser assets, including call content, in Local Services (April 2025 terms).
leads.why_not_a_claim: Not opened; could give the April 2025 terms change in a news source.

not_found.question: Q3
not_found.what: Google's own statement of what the advertiser hears (any whisper or announcement) on a recorded Google Ads call-ad, call-asset or website call. Only the Local Services 'Call from Google' message is documented.

not_found.question: Q4
not_found.what: A current Google statement of how long Google Ads call recordings are kept after the 2026 default change. The only figure is 30 days on the older 'Play your call recordings' page; no period for legal is stated for Google Ads.

not_found.question: Q6
not_found.what: Any setting that lets a Local Services Ads provider turn off call recording. I found none in Google's Local Services help pages or terms; the terms make authorizing recording a condition of use.

not_found.question: Q7
not_found.what: Any Google page that names legal services as excluded from call recording (Ads or Local Services). Excluded: healthcare and financial services (Ads, by default); health care and tax specialists (Local Services). Legal appears on the Local Services retention line, which implies it is recorded.

not_found.question: Q1
not_found.what: A Google statement on Local Services Ads recording in countries other than the US and Canada. Only the North America sections say recordings exist; the 'outside North America' section lists number, time and duration only.

not_found.question: Q8
not_found.what: A formal state bar ethics opinion that names Google call recording from Local Services Ads or Google Ads call assets. Found only a Wisconsin ethics-counsel article (2021) and a withdrawn North Carolina proposed opinion (2021, withdrawn April 2022). Nothing from the Florida, Texas, California, Virginia or Pennsylvania bars was found.

not_found.question: Q9
not_found.what: First-hand public threads by lawyers, law firm staff or their marketers about Google recording these calls (Reddit, Google Ads Community, Lawyerist, Local Search Forum). Reddit was inaccessible; searches of the Local Search Forum, Google Ads Community and lawyer forums returned no matching thread.

not_found.question: Q10
not_found.what: A clause requiring the advertiser to tell or get consent from callers specifically. The terms speak of 'any other party that may participate in the Communications' and Google plays its own caller notice; no separate caller-consent clause was found.
